name: Milesian School
description: Material monists searching for the primary substrate (arche) of the cosmos.

name: Eleatic School
description: Parmenidean metaphysics of immutable, indivisible Being and the illusion of change.

name: Ancient Atomism
description: Democritus and Leucippus: the universe consists entirely of indivisible atoms moving through the void.

name: Platonism
description: Dualistic metaphysics of immaterial, immutable Forms contrasted with the sensory realm of shadows.

name: Aristotelianism
description: Empirical naturalism, hylomorphism (matter and form), teleology, and virtue ethics.

name: Stoicism
description: Virtue as the sole good, living in accordance with Nature/Logos, and mastering inner impressions.

name: Epicureanism
description: Hedonism refined: pleasure as the absence of pain and mental anxiety (ataraxia).

name: Pyrrhonian Skepticism
description: Epoché (suspension of judgment) as the royal road to unshakeable tranquility.

name: Neoplatonism
description: Hierarchical emanation from the ineffable 'One' through Nous and Soul down to material existence.

name: Eastern Non-Dualism & Dao
description: Buddhism, Daoism, and Advaita Vedanta exploring the nature of consciousness, emptiness, and harmony.

name: Scholasticism
description: Methodical synthesis of Christian revelation with Aristotelian logic and metaphysics.

name: Falsafa (Islamic Philosophy)
description: Ibn Sina, Al-Farabi, and Ibn Rushd preserving, expanding, and refining Hellenistic philosophy.

name: Continental Rationalism
description: Intellectual intuition and deduction from innate ideas as the primary source of knowledge (Descartes, Spinoza, Leibniz).

name: British Empiricism
description: All knowledge originates in sensory experience (Locke, Berkeley, Hume).

name: Social Contract & Enlightenment
description: Political legitimacy derived from the governed; human autonomy and critique of prejudice.

name: German Idealism
description: Transcendental idealism (Kant) and Absolute Idealism (Hegel): mind constructing reality.

name: 19th c. Existential & Radical Thought
description: Critique of grand systematic philosophy; focus on individual passion, alienation, and will.

name: Utilitarianism
description: Consequentialist ethics maximizing happiness and minimizing suffering for the greatest number.

name: American Pragmatism
description: The meaning and truth of an idea reside in its practical, experiential consequences.

name: Phenomenology
description: Direct investigation of conscious experience and structures of phenomena 'to the things themselves'.

name: Existentialism
description: Existence precedes essence: radical freedom, anxiety, bad faith, and the creation of personal meaning.

name: Analytic Philosophy & Logic
description: Conceptual clarification through formal logic, linguistics, and critique of metaphysical pseudo-problems.

name: Frankfurt School & Critical Theory
description: Critique of modern rationalization, cultural commodification, and capitalist alienation.

name: Post-Structuralism & Contemporary
description: Decentering the subject, deconstruction of binary hierarchies, surveillance, biopolitics, and simulation.
